name: Once Upon a Nursery Shelf: Children's Classics
description: Fairy tales, bears, wizards and cartoon mice: the stories and characters that grew up with generations of children, from the Brothers Grimm to Harry Potter.

checkpoints.name: Tales by the fire
checkpoints.note: The Brothers Grimm gather folk tales, Hans Christian Andersen writes new ones, and in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland Lewis Carroll sends a girl down a rabbit hole. The Adventures of Pinocchio shows a wooden puppet learning to be real.

checkpoints.name: Bears, wizards and mice
checkpoints.note: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz opens the Land of Oz and Peter Pan refuses to grow up. Winnie-the-Pooh, Mickey Mouse and Tintin follow in the 1920s, and Donald Duck quacks in 1934, as books, films and comics reach younger readers.

checkpoints.name: The golden age of the cartoon
checkpoints.note: Walt Disney makes Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs, and The Wizard of Oz film follows in 1939, while Bugs Bunny and The Beano appear. The Hobbit, The Little Prince and The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe bring wonder, Charlie and the Chocolate Factory adds mischief, and Peanuts, Snoopy, Asterix, Astro Boy and Doraemon charm readers.

checkpoints.name: From puppet to pixel
checkpoints.note: Sesame Street, on air since late 1969, teaches by television and The Muppet Show makes puppets stars. Hello Kitty becomes a pocket-sized star, Toy Story and The Lion King set new heights, and J. K. Rowling's Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone begins a wizard craze that runs into the new century.
